newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Lawyers, doctors join Rasta bid to legalize pot.
newsitem.headline: Lawyers, doctors join Rasta bid to legalize pot.

text.p: Jamaica's Rastafarians marshalled the support of doctors, lawyers, and even an English lord on Wednesday in their bid to decriminalize marijuana on the island.
The Rastafarians, a homegrown religion which worships the late Ethopian Emperor Haile Selassie as God, regularly use marijuana or "ganja" during their rituals.

Local Rasta leaders have launched the Legalise Ganja Campaign, saying they have been in continuous conflict with the authorities to the point where 80 percent of the local Rasta community have criminal records for drug possession.
At a news briefing on Wednesday, several professionals said they backed them.
Dr. Ronald Lampart, a medical practitioner who has researched ganja's effects on humans, said he has not found a single case of death caused directly by ganja use.
Ganja is less addictive than alcohol or tobacco, both of which are legal, he added.

"Why do we arrest every youth found smoking ganja?" the doctor asked, saying most wind up in Jamaica's notoriously overcrowded prisons. "They are creating criminals out of these young people and by creating criminals they will not be able to control crime."
Lawyer Lord Anthony Gifford, a member of the British House of Lords, said the campaign would run for as long as the government took to change laws.

Despite government pledges in the 1970s to consider decriminalizing the possession of small amounts of marijuana, the anti-drug stance has hardened. National Security Minister K.D. Knight said on Wednesday his government had no intention of considering such a move, stating: "What we cannot do is contribute to a drug culture."

The pro-ganja lobby was launched as Jamaica prepared to begin negotiating a drug interdiction treaty with the United States on Friday. The treaty will give U.S. officials permission to pursue and apprehend suspected drug traffickers in Jamaica's 188-square mile (480-square km) exclusive economic zone.
The U.S. government has identified Jamaica as the largest grower and exporter of marijuana in the Caribbean.
